page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. The instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-level acceleration features include AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 vector and matrix extensions, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a direct-attached 945 GB NVMe solid-state drive, augmenting remote storage capabilities with fast temporary scratch disk performance. The server lacks dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs, directing all compute and matrix operations through the host CPU instruction sets. Networking operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network interfaces and private IP configurations by default.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within the median performance bracket for standard compute tasks, recording a PassMark CPU score of 27,311.65 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 16,997.20. Compression and decompression tests show stronger relative capabilities, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 35.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 14.92 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory read throughput measures 129.38 GB/sec alongside 54.82 GB/sec write throughput. For quantized AI inference, the platform delivers 354.35 tokens per second on text generation using a small 135M model, utilizing Intel AMX capabilities.

This hardware balance makes the D16ds_v7 suited for enterprise relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving architectures, CI/CD runners, and batch ETL pipelines requiring moderate memory capacity and low-latency local NVMe scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 945 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions alongside an expansive 480 MB L3 cache, omitting dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluation shows consistent median-tier CPU and memory performance, complemented by upper-quartile data compression throughput and strong execution speeds for small-model language inference. With a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and high-speed temporary storage, the D16ds_v7 is suited for medium-tier relational database systems, in-memory key-value caching, software build runners, and enterprise web serving stacks.
